header: Test vectors for HPKE (RFC 9180) single-shot Open in base mode
using the ML-KEM-1024 KEM from draft-ietf-hpke-pq. The recipient
private key skRm is the 64-byte d || z seed. Valid cases include
ikmE, the 32-byte encapsulation randomness, so deterministic
encapsulation reproduces enc and ct. Given (skRm, info, aad, enc,
ct) an implementation runs SetupBaseR then Open and must recover
pt for valid cases or reject invalid cases. See doc/hpke.md.

AllZeroEnc.description: enc is all-zero (correct length). ML-KEM decapsulates it via implicit rejection to an unrelated shared secret, so Open must fail.

AppendedByteCiphertext.description: A trailing byte was appended to the AEAD ciphertext.

EmbeddedZeroAad.description: The AEAD associated data contains embedded zero bytes.

EmbeddedZeroInfo.description: The HPKE info contains embedded zero bytes, catching a consumer that mishandles them (e.g. treats info as null-terminated).

EmbeddedZeroPlaintext.description: The plaintext contains embedded zero bytes.

EmptyAad.description: The AEAD associated data is empty.

EmptyCiphertext.description: The AEAD ciphertext is empty (shorter than one tag).

EmptyInfo.description: The HPKE info string is empty.

LongPlaintext.description: A 512-byte plaintext, exercising the AEAD across multiple blocks.

MismatchedEncCt.description: enc and ct come from two different encapsulations to the same recipient, so the AEAD key derived from enc does not match the one that sealed ct; Open must fail.

ModifiedCiphertext.description: A bit of the AEAD ciphertext body was flipped.

ModifiedEnc.description: A bit of the KEM encapsulation enc was flipped. ML-KEM implicit rejection (FIPS 203) yields a different shared secret, so Open must fail at the AEAD tag check.

ModifiedTag.description: A bit of the AEAD authentication tag was flipped.

Pseudorandom.description: A valid HPKE base-mode ciphertext with deterministic encapsulation from ikmE (draft-ietf-hpke-pq Section 3).

SeedAllOnes.description: The recipient private key is the all-one (0xFF) 64-byte seed; key derivation must succeed and be deterministic.

SeedAllZero.description: The recipient private key is the all-zero 64-byte seed. Every 64-byte string is a valid ML-KEM d || z seed (FIPS 203), so key derivation must succeed and be deterministic.

TruncatedCiphertext.description: The AEAD ciphertext is truncated below the tag length.

WrongAad.description: The aad differs from the one sealed under; accepting it would bypass AEAD authentication of the associated data.

WrongInfo.description: The info differs from the one sealed under, so the key schedule derives a different key; accepting it would bypass the info binding (RFC 9180 Section 5.1).

WrongLengthEnc.description: enc does not have the KEM's Nenc length (empty, short, long, or the length of a different ML-KEM parameter set) and must be rejected by SetupBaseR.

WrongRecipientEnc.description: enc and ct are a valid encapsulation and sealing for a different recipient key. Decapsulating under this skRm yields a different shared secret, so Open must fail.
